deployment.commit_message:
GAP-FILL: dedupe auto-register-product-modules.js registry by path to prevent double-mounting

Tried: found 6 files in config/auto-registered-product-modules.json
with two registry entries at once (boldtrail-routes.js, curriculumRoutes.js,
issueApprovalRoutes.js with both entries enabled:true; 3 more with
one enabled + one disabled). Exact gap: startup/auto-register-product-modules.js's
registration loop has zero path-based dedup -- confirmed by reading it
directly. For files whose register function mounts routes via
app.post/app.get directly on the shared app (not a scoped sub-router
-- confirmed for boldtrail-routes.js), two enabled entries means the
real handler gets mounted and runs twice per matching request, a real
duplicate-write risk on revenue-facing routes. Already fixed
boldtrail-routes.js's duplicate once this session (commit 07ef5b1d2)
and it recurred within the hour from a different BUILD_QUEUE step's
independent registry write -- config-file firefighting doesn't scale
against this rate of recurrence.

Hardened the loader itself: dedupe by path, keep the last *enabled*
entry, only fall back to a disabled entry if every entry for that path
is disabled (verified this ordering matters -- 2 of the 6 files have
their enabled:true entry listed BEFORE their enabled:false entry, so
a naive "last wins" dedup would have silently disabled a working
registration; simulated the fix against the live registry data to
confirm all 6 resolve correctly with zero accidental disables before
shipping). Existing test suite (tests/auto-register-product-modules.test.js)
still passes 4/4.

HAND-AUTHORED-JUSTIFICATION: a bounded, deterministic bug fix (dedupe
an array before an existing loop) to existing boot/startup
orchestration logic, not new business logic or a new module -- tested
against both the real registry data and the existing test suite before
shipping.
